entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is the relation whereby a norm or rule attaches a duty to a specific bearer (the agent). In BFO terms this is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in the agent (its bearer), is externally grounded in the normative/legal system that imposes the obligation, and is realizable in the agent's compliant or non-compliant behaviour. It is distinct from the content of the obligation itself (which is a generically dependent continuant, e.g. a subtype of LegalObligation as information) and from the process of performing the obligated act. The existing class LegalObligation is already typed as BFO_0000023 (Role); AgentObligationBinding can be modelled as a subclass of LegalObligation that specifically emphasises the binding relation between the norm and its bearer-agent.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a more specific kind of LegalObligation (which is already typed as BFO_0000023/Role). It refines LegalObligation by emphasising the binding of a norm to a specific agent-bearer, making it a natural subclass rather than a sibling class.
Explicit assertion that AgentObligationBinding is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023), confirming its BFO type for the reasoner.

open_questions: Should AgentObligationBinding be restricted to legal/institutional agents only, or should it cover moral obligations to individual persons as well? This affects whether it should be a subclass of LegalObligation or a sibling of it under BFO_0000023.

Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended as a class of role-instances (one per agent-norm pair), or as a relational quality between two entities? If the latter, a custom object property or a BFO_0000019 Quality subclass might be more appropriate than a Role.

Should AgentObligationBinding carry a disposition (BFO_0000016) sub-part representing the agent's capacity to comply? If so, an associated DispositionToComply class could be linked via BFO_0000051 (has part).

Is there a specific normative theory (Kelsenian, Hartian, Finnisian) presupposed by the user that would constrain the grounding conditions of this binding? This would affect which existing individuals (e.g., Grundnorm, ValidityOntologicalPrimacyThesis) should be linked to instances of AgentObligationBinding.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' denotes the fact that a normative rule attaches a duty to a specific agent as its bearer. In BFO 2020 this maps most naturally to the Role category (BFO_0000023): roles are specifically dependent continuants that inhere in bearers and are externally grounded — precisely the structure of an obligation that binds an agent because of a norm external to the agent. The existing working class LegalObligation already carries this typing (BFO_0000023), so AgentObligationBinding is proposed as a new subclass of LegalObligation that makes the agent-binding aspect explicit. A relation rdfs:subClassOf to both LegalObligation and BFO_0000023 is asserted. Several open questions are raised because the precise intended meaning — whether this is a role-instance, a relational quality, or something tied to a specific normative theory — will determine whether the typing should be adjusted or additional structure (e.g., a linked disposition or a quality) should be added.
